newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CAP MKTS HEAD SAYS MONITOR OF EPEYS IS DIFFICULT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CAP MKTS HEAD SAYS MONITOR OF EPEYS IS DIFFICULT.

text.p: The chairman of Greece's capital markets commission, Stavros Thomadakis, told reporters that the commission lacked adequate human resources to fully monitor the activities of new investment services firms (EPEYS).

"The capital markets commission has not even a fraction of the Bank of Greece's supervisory capabilites," said Thomadakis. "Our human resources are limited but the new law (about EPEYs) will go into effect."
The law 2396/96 was voted in parliament last April and outlines the general framework governing the activities of firms offering investment services in Greece.
He added that the commission was going to beef up its staff to enhance its market monitoring capabilities.

Thomadakis made public three regulations concerning the implementation of Law 2396/96. The law embodies the directive of European Council on investment services and harmonises Greek legislation with that of the European Union.
The first regulation refers to the necessary conditions that firms (EPEYS) with equity capital of "200 million or one billion drachmas" should meet to be given a licence to operate.
The second regulation refers to bookkeeping by EPEYs falling outside the current tax code.

"The main goal of the requested figures is the ability of the investor and the supervisory authority to look into the transactions of the firm (EPEY) and confirm that investors' orders have been executed."

The third regulation refers to Greek depository receipts (ELPIS) and sets the criteria for granting a licence to credit institutions that issue ELPIS. ELPIS is the Greek version of U.S ADRs. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
